question: Do installed original provider executables select their matching original script/test support under the shared source-tree execution environment?
scope: setup/pairing acceptance only; no semantic conformance or unmeasured capability claim

providers.support_selection: explicitly sources the original tree tcltest.tcl in file mode; embedded initjimsh/tclcompat input hashes retained separately

argv: puts [info patchlevel]; puts [info nameofexecutable]; puts [info commands info]; puts [package require tcltest]

negative_setup_surface.expected_limitation: Jim -e has no argv0; original tcltest.tcl source refuses before setup completes

limitations: Only setup, identity and explicit script/test support pairing were executed; no command-name or runtime semantics were tested.
Named source/support files and static archives are hashed; existing immutable C input inventories are validated by reference without duplicating their file lists; no source/binary copy is retained.
C source tags come from the shared reference manifest; existing immutable compiler-source integrity records are reused where available, and matching init hashes are checked independently.
Hashing a static archive records its installed build input; it is not a reproducible-build proof that the entire archive was linked.
Jim startup support is embedded in the executable; initjimsh/tclcompat generated-C and original Tcl inputs are hashed, without a separate native execution proof for each helper.
The historical shared-owner PASS log is independent supporting evidence, not substituted for these actual process captures.
